Common edge options

Choose edge types and configure appearance, labels, interactions, parallel edges, and routing

View source on GitHub

Use GraphOptions.edge to choose a path and configure the line, arrows, and labels. See Edge overview for endpoints, direction, and edge data.

EdgeConfig

EdgeConfig is the edge option passed to new Graph(). This example draws a blue line with a target arrow and uses purple when the edge is selected.

PropertyDescriptionTypeDefaultRequired
typeBuilt-in edge type or registered custom edge namestring'line'No
styleLine, path parameters, arrows, and labelsEdgeConfig['style']Theme and built-in stylesNo
stateStylesAppearance overrides by statePartial<Record<EdgeState, EdgeStateStyleOverride>>Extension or theme state stylesNo
parallelEdgesSeparate edges with the same endpointsboolean | ParallelEdgesConfigDisabledNo
labelRendererRegistered label rendererstringBuilt-in label rendererNo

Specify the edge type

Set edge.type to specify the edge type. The default is line. This example uses polyline for all edges in the graph.

Type valueNameUse
lineStraight lineConnect endpoints directly
arcArcControl the bend or separate edges with the same endpoints
cubicCubic BézierConnect horizontal levels with a smooth curve
polylinePolylineRoute connections in flowcharts, directory trees, or fishbone diagrams

Register a custom edge before using its name as edge.type.

Line edges

line connects the endpoints directly. Set endArrow: true to draw an arrow at the target.

Arcs and cubic curves

Arc edges

Use curvature to control which way and how far the arc bends. Compare -0.35, 0, and 0.35 below.

Cubic edges

curveOffset sets the horizontal handles of a cubic edge. Compare 30 and 120 below. The path may remain straight when the endpoints share a height.

Style

Edge path styles

Line styles control an edge’s color, width, opacity, and direction.

FieldTypeDefault or fallbackMeaning
strokeEdgeStyleValue<string>theme.edgeStroke; light '#99ADD1', dark '#637088'Edge and arrow color
lineWidthEdgeStyleValue<number>theme.edgeLineWidth, preset 1Visual width; use a finite positive value
opacityEdgeStyleValue<number>1Opacity from 0 to 1
lineDashEdgeStyleValue<number[]>[]Empty means solid; the current period uses the sum of the first two values, as described in Dash rules
startArrowEdgeStyleValue<boolean>falseSource-end arrow pointing toward source
endArrowEdgeStyleValue<boolean>theme.edgeArrow, true in both light and darkTarget-end arrow pointing toward target
arrowSizeEdgeStyleValue<number>Derived from line widthLength along the path; use a finite positive explicit length. Nonpositive values use automatic length
hitAreaWidthEdgeStyleValue<number>Final lineWidthTotal picking width, independent of visual width; see Picking width

Line width, hit width, arrow length, and dash periods stay fixed in screen-rendering pixels as the graph zooms.

Style functions

Style functions receive (source, target, edge) and use each edge’s data to set its appearance. The preview maps edge.data to thin solid, dashed, and bidirectional edges.

Dash rules

Use lineDash to draw a dashed edge. Its first two values add up to the dash period. This example uses a lineWidth of 3 to compare a solid line and two dash spacings.

Arrows

Use startArrow and endArrow to control arrows at both ends and arrowSize to set their length.

Arrow sizes and defaults

Hit area

Use hitAreaWidth to widen the area that detects pointer input while keeping the stroke width. This example enables selection with click-select.

State styles

Use edge.stateStyles to set appearance by state. Click an edge to see its purple selection style.

Parallel-edge spacing

Separate multiple relationships between the same two nodes with parallel edges. A self-loop connects a node to itself.

Separate same-direction and reverse edges

Use edge.parallelEdges to separate overlapping edges between the same two nodes. The top row shows three A→B edges and a purple self-loop on B. The bottom row shows a pair in opposite directions.

Adjust parallel-edge spacing and grouping

Set edge.parallelEdges in new Graph() to enable separation and configure it. This works with line and arc.

  • Spacing. Click Spacing 24 / 64 above and compare the three A→B edges. Increasing offset from 24 to 64 makes the two outer edges bend farther apart.
  • Grouping. includeReverse: true puts C→D and D→C in the same group, separating them. Click Toggle reverse group to set it to false. Each edge forms its own group and the pair overlaps in the example.

After rendering, use updateOptions() to change the spacing. It replaces the entire parallelEdges object, so include the settings you want to keep.

See ParallelEdgesConfig for units, offset limits, and grouping rules.

Configure parallel edges in transforms

If you configure data processing in transforms, process-parallel-edges gives you the same behavior. Either option works on its own.

If you set the same option in both places, edge.parallelEdges takes priority. With offset: 48 in the edge config and offset: 24 in the transform, the graph uses 48. Set edge.parallelEdges to false to turn separation off.

Add or remove parallel edges

When parallel-edge separation is enabled, adding or removing an edge automatically rearranges the edges in its group. Click Add ab4 above to add a fourth A→B edge. The existing edges move to make room.

Click Remove ab4 to delete the new edge and return to three A→B edges.

Self-loops and labels

Set source and target to the same node to draw a loop. Drag a node to see its loops and labels move with it.

The renderer sets loop sizes and levels. parallelEdges spacing applies to edges between distinct endpoints.

Polyline routing

Set edge.type: 'polyline', then choose a path with router. See EdgeConfig.style for fields and defaults.

Choose a router

RouterUse
orthFlowcharts. Connects endpoints with horizontal and vertical segments and supports radius
treeHierarchies. Assigns ports to edges from the same source and draws smooth curves
indentedDirectory trees. Connects children to a parent trunk
fishboneFishbone diagrams. Pair with the fishbone layout

Orthogonal connections and rounding

Orthogonal edges use horizontal and vertical segments. Set Radius to 0 for square corners or 16 for rounded corners.

Indented directory connections

Pair the indented layout and router to connect children to a parent trunk. The example sets direction: 'LR'.

Adjust indentation and row spacing with layout.indent and layout.rowHeight.

Choose where edges meet child nodes

In a horizontal directory tree, set indentTarget to left to connect to the side of the child rectangle closest to its parent, as shown above.

For text-only child nodes, use right to extend the line to the end of the text. Switch between 有背景 (with background) and 无样式 (text only) in the indented tree example to see both options.

Set the direction of polylines

Polylines follow the layout direction. For Dagre, rankdir: 'LR' goes left to right and rankdir: 'TB' goes top to bottom. Use Direction in the orthogonal connections example to compare them.

For the indented layout, direction: 'LR' indents to the right and direction: 'RL' indents to the left.

Edge labels

Set the relationship name with edge.style.label and its position along the edge with labelPlacement. The preview compares labels near the start, in the middle, and near the end.

FieldTypeDefault and rules
labelEdgeStyleValue<string | false>false; only nonempty strings render, while empty strings or false hide the label
labelFontSizeEdgeStyleValue<number>10 screen pixels; use a finite positive value
labelFontFamilyEdgeStyleValue<string>System sans-serif stack
labelColorEdgeStyleValue<string>'#666', independent of line color
labelPlacementEdgeStyleValue<'start' | 'center' | 'end'>'center'; path parameters t = 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8, not exact endpoints
labelBackgroundEdgeStyleValue<string | false>'rgba(255,255,255,0.8)'; false disables the background
labelBackgroundPaddingEdgeStyleValue<number>2 screen pixels around the background; use a finite nonnegative value
labelAutoRotateEdgeStyleValue<boolean>true; follow the tangent while keeping text upright. false keeps text horizontal

Label background styles

Set the background with labelBackground and its padding with labelBackgroundPadding. The start label above has its background turned off.

Position and visibility

Labels on cubic and polyline edges use the line between endpoints for position and rotation. Font size stays fixed. Visibility follows global label policies and the hidden state of the edge and its endpoints.

labelRenderer

Set edge.labelRenderer to choose how labels are drawn. The demo-multiline renderer below draws the protocol and request type on separate lines.

See Custom Label Renderer to implement and register a renderer.

Develop a custom edge

Use an EdgeExtension to package a reusable path and appearance. See Custom edges for registration, configuration, and a runnable example.

Update edges dynamically

Update one edge’s data or change the graph-wide style after rendering. Lower SQL latency updates the SQL edge, and Set edge color recolors both edges.

See updateEdgeData() and updateOptions() for more operations.

Common questions

Why do parallel edges still overlap?

Check that enabled is true and the type is line or arc, then check maxOffset and includeReverse.

Why does offset not resize self-loops?

The renderer sizes self-loops. offset controls parallel-edge spacing.

Why is a thin line still difficult to select?

Use hitAreaWidth with an interaction such as click-select.

Why is a label missing?

Check that edge.style.label returns text, then check zoom, collisions, and whether the edge or an endpoint is hidden.

Why doesn't changing the router at runtime work?

After setting a new router with updateOptions(), call render() to rebuild the polyline paths.

Why does an edge cross another node?

orth routes from the two endpoints. Adjust layout or node spacing to keep edges clear of other nodes.

Why does a configured state not activate?

Activate the state with a behavior or setItemState(edgeId, state, true).

Why does a line miss the node boundary?

Check node dimensions, layout nodeSize, and direction. Use indentTarget: 'left' for rectangles in horizontal directory trees.

Why does the label not follow the polyline?

polyline labels use the line between endpoints for position and rotation.
